To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the trigeminal Me5 nucleus, which is located in the brainstem, contains neurons that encode the kinematic properties (direction, velocity, amplitude) of spontaneous movements of the whisker macrovibrissæ; (b) these Me5 whisking neurons, whose number seems to correspond to that of the whisker pads macrovibrissal follicles, are organized in a single cluster located in the medial‐ caudal part of this nucleus; (c)
the trigeminal Me5 neurons are involved in encoding the whisker pad movements.
the Me5 neurons encode the kinematic properties (direction, amplitude, frequency, and velocity) of the whisker macrovibrissal movements.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the trigeminal system, and particularly of the Me5, which is a nucleus that has received relatively little attention in the literature.
the role of the trigeminal nuclei in the control of the whisker‐pad movements.
the study of the trigeminal nuclei, and more specifically with the trigeminal Me5 nucleus, as an important component of the somatic sensorimotor system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, besides the trigeminal brainstem nuclei involved in encoding tactile and nociceptive inputs, Me5 neurons are likely involved in encoding proprioception, which is a key feature of the trigeminal system.

the Me5 nucleus is a part of a complex system of the trigeminal sensory nuclei, which, besides the sensory information related to the mechanical deflection of whisker pad, is also involved in the proprioception of whisker pad movements.

the trigeminal system is a multisensory system, and that its sensory information is not only conveyed by the primary afferents but is also processed by the trigeminal nuclei, and that, in turn, these nuclei are not only sensory but are also motor nuclei.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the trigeminal nuclei, in particular the mesencephalic one, are involved in processing both tactile and proprioceptive information arising in the whiskers and whisking movements, and that this is a common property of the somatosensory system.
the Me5 neurons, which represent the whisker pad vibrissae, are involved in encoding the proprioceptive information arising during spontaneous and voluntary whisker pad macro‐vibrissae movement.

the Me5 neurons, in addition to their role in proprioceptive transmission of whisker pad tactile information, are also involved in the proprioceptive transmission of kinematic information related to the macrovibrissa movements.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, as for the trigemina ganglion, the Me5 nucleus contains a representation of the whisking movements of the macrovibrisae, and that the Me5 whisker pad neurons are involved in encoding the whisker pad kinematic properties.

Me5 neurons, besides encoding the whisker pad displacement per se, also encode the kinematic properties (velocity, acceleration, etc.) of the whisker macrovibrissal movements, thus representing a key element in the encoding of the whisker kinematics.
the Me5 nucleus represents a key component for the encoding of proprioceptive information related to the whisking behavior. Environ. Entomol. 39(4): 1041–1052, 2010
